{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the data
sales = pd.read_csv('data/sales.csv')

# Clean the revenue column: remove commas and convert to float
sales['revenue_clean'] = sales['revenue'].str.replace(',', '', regex=False).astype(float)

# Identify QA orders (revenue == 999999.99)
qa_orders = sales[sales['revenue_clean'] == 999999.99]

# Check if these QA orders have valid customer_age and converted status
print("QA orders details:")
print(qa_orders[['order_id', 'customer_age', 'converted']].to_string(index=False))

# Check if any QA orders have non-null customer_age
qa_with_age = qa_orders['customer_age'].notna().sum()
print(f"Number of QA orders with non-null customer_age: {qa_with_age}")

# Since the question is about mean age of converted customers, we only care if QA orders are in the converted group and have valid age
# If they are not converted or have missing age, they do not affect the mean age of converted customers
qa_converted = qa_orders['converted'].sum()
print(f"Number of QA orders that were converted: {qa_converted}")

# If QA orders are not in the converted group or have missing age, they do not affect the mean age of converted customers
# But if they are converted and have age, they would bias the mean
assert qa_converted == 0, "QA orders should not be converted""}
